currentContext.business: Kaynes designs and manufactures complex electronic assemblies, sub-systems and box-builds for global and domestic OEMs and Tier I partners, with capabilities spanning conceptual design and embedded engineering, PCB assembly, product engineering and end-to-end lifecycle support. It serves high-reliability sectors including Automotive, Industrial and EV, Railways, Medical, Aerospace and Defence, and IoT/IT/Consumer, specialising in high-mix, high-value and complex mechatronic assemblies. The Company is extending backward into bare-board multilayer HDI PCB fabrication at Chennai and into semiconductor assembly, testing and packaging (OSAT) at Sanand, Gujarat, to deliver an integrated 'silicon-to-system' offering.

currentContext.expansion: Kaynes' FY 2025-26 expansion programme centred on two greenfield initiatives that moved from planning to execution. The Sanand OSAT facility was operationalised and delivered India's first commercially manufactured Multi-Chip Module (IPM5) in collaboration with global partners; the Company also received the Financial Support Agreement under the India Semiconductor Mission, giving visibility on central and state capital subsidies and improving cash-flow certainty. Total capex earmarked for OSAT is Rs 33,070 Mn, materially de-risked by the FSA, with eligible support of a 50% central subsidy and a 20% state subsidy on allowable capex of Rs 26,150 Mn. In parallel, the multilayer HDI PCB facility at Chennai is nearing completion and is designed to manufacture complex boards of up to 74 layers for defence, aerospace and strategic electronics applications; Phase 1 capex for the Chennai facility is Rs 14,000 Mn, described as government-approved capex targeted for South India, and is expected to unlock synergies between bare-board production and electronic system assembly. Together these position the Company to offer an integrated 'silicon-to-system' solution. Capital allocation in the core EMS business is deliberately selective — deployed for debottlenecking, focused on improving asset turnover, and avoiding a build-up of redundant capacity. The Company states it is adequately funded through internal accruals and previous QIP raises and does not intend to undertake further equity dilution to execute its immediate expansion phases. Footprint additions also came inorganically and through capability build-out: the integration of August Electronics in Canada established a credible manufacturing footprint in North America in RF microwave assemblies; a strategic collaboration with Infineon opened entry into MEMS-based True Wireless Stereo packaging; the Kochi plant runs high-volume manufacturing of client computing devices; and the Chamarajanagara plant participates in India's PARAM Supercomputer Mission through the high-end Rudra server. In the smart-utility business, GridCrest has deployed meter-to-cash solutions for about 2.50 Mn smart meters across Gujarat, Kerala, West Bengal, Nagaland and Madhya Pradesh, and its platform is described as globally scalable with planned entry into European markets.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption, import dependence and single-sourcing
risks.note: Over-reliance on imported customer-referred parts and the absence of reliable local sourcing partners may disrupt production cycles and delay customer deliveries, while inflationary commodity prices and import freight charges pressure margins. Mitigation rests on backward integration into OSAT and bare-board PCB manufacturing, strategic safety stock and Vendor-Managed Inventory programmes targeting 10 suppliers in FY 2026-27.

Trade barriers, tariff fluctuations and concentrated geographic dependencies could disrupt access to essential electronic materials or technologies, lengthening lead times and raising freight costs. The Company is progressively reducing the proportion of procurement from China for relays, transformers, inductors and connectors, and diversifying through the August Electronics acquisition in North America and export enablement from the Sanand and Chennai facilities.

Rapid technological shifts could render manufacturing processes redundant and cost market share in high-margin verticals such as aerospace and defence. Mitigation is continuous R&D investment, a shift to a product-led ESDM model with growing ODM contribution, proprietary IP including Kavach and high-performance computing platforms, and investment in 74-layer HDI PCBs, silicon photonics, co-packaged optics and MEMS-based solutions.

risks.risk: Execution and project scale-up risk in new greenfield verticals
risks.note: Near-term revenue shortfalls and execution 'hiccups' can arise from deferral of safety-critical projects such as the Kavach railway programme or delays in pilot clearances, while entry into OSAT and HDI PCB manufacturing may face setup or coordination delays affecting go-to-market timelines. Mitigation includes operationalising the Sanand OSAT facility, nearing completion of the Chennai HDI PCB plant, transplanting proven process parameters with global machinery and material-science experts, and early engagement with marquee anchor customers.

risks.risk: Working capital intensity and financial volatility
risks.note: High-growth phases and custom-built orders drive elevated inventory and receivables, pressuring earnings through cash-conversion swings. The response is supply chain finance, bill discounting, inventory optimisation, consolidated buying, monetisation of legacy receivables, a dedicated collections team targeting positive consolidated operating cash flow, DSO and DIO improvement of 10-15% year on year, and a targeted net working capital cycle towards 100 days.

risks.risk: Policy and regulatory dependency on government incentives
risks.note: Large-scale greenfield expansions and incentive eligibility are structurally dependent on policy shifts and timely disbursement of grants; failure to comply could mean financial penalties, loss of PLI eligibility or reduced government-linked incentives. Mitigation includes securing the India Semiconductor Mission Financial Support Agreement, a dedicated compliance team for ISM requirements, monthly tracking with ministries, contingency financing and Board-level oversight.

Product failures, regulatory penalties or reporting inconsistencies and disclosure errors could cost critical OEM trust and certifications and erode stakeholder confidence. Controls include a zero-compromise quality approach, Total Productive Maintenance (rolled out at two plants), Poke-Yoke, MES interlinking across sites, internal compliance and audit review processes integrated in the ERP system, enhanced disclosure validation and software-driven reconciliation controls. OEE improvement targets stand at 75% for FY 2026-27 and 80% for FY 2027-28, tracked monthly.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data privacy as digital systems scale
risks.note: Inadequate cyber security infrastructure and data protection could expose the Company to data breaches, IP loss, system disruption, regulatory penalties and reputational damage — identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a negative-implication risk. Mitigation is IT security policies, access control, physical and logical security, continuous monitoring, ERP-driven automation of financial and operational data flows, and enterprise-wide system standardisation.

risks.risk: Talent attrition and skill gaps during rapid expansion
risks.note: Rapid scaling into high-tech verticals such as OSAT risks operational disruption and loss of institutional knowledge. Mitigation includes structured leadership pipelines, internal talent mobility, collaboration with global experts to transfer advanced technical capabilities, and strengthening TPM culture.

risks.risk: Deployment bottlenecks in the smart-metering / project business
risks.note: Client-side operational or logistical misalignment can delay billing or revenue realisation even after components are manufactured and delivered on time. The Company is pivoting away from project implementation (AMISP) towards being a high-volume device and solution provider to shorten the realisation cycle.

one-line thesis: Kaynes delivered strong 33% revenue growth and 39.8% EBITDA growth in FY26 despite near-term revenue misses due to geopolitical delays and metering execution lags, but strategically pivoted toward product-driven revenue (30% target) via OSAT, PCB, and smart metering, with order book at INR9,000cr and cash flow normalization expected within 3 quarters.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift of the global industry from build-to-print EMS towards integrated ESDM spanning R&D, product design, manufacturing, testing and full lifecycle management, with the global ESDM market projected to reach US$ 1,203 Bn by CY 2027 at a 5.2% CAGR from CY 2021
- Global EMS market valued at US$ 648.11 Bn in FY 2024-25 and projected to reach nearly US$ 1.20 Tn by 2034, with India emerging as a preferred manufacturing hub
- Indian ESDM market expected to double to Rs 7-8 Lakh Crores by CY 2030 at a 20-25% CAGR from CY 2025, with domestic electronics production at Rs 11.30 Lakh Crores in FY 2024-25 and electronics now India's third-largest and fastest-growing export category
- Policy stack driving upstream localisation — PLI, SPECS (25% capital expenditure incentive), EMC 2.0, the Phased Manufacturing Programme, and the ECMS outlay raised to Rs 40,000 Crores from Rs 22,919 Crores in the Union Budget 2026-27, channelling investment into bare-board PCB and component ecosystems
- Semicon India Programme with an outlay of Rs 76,000 Crores, plus an allocation of Rs 760 Bn towards semiconductor and display fabrication; the Indian semiconductor market at about US$ 45-50 Bn in 2024-25 is projected to cross US$ 100-110 Bn by 2030 and reach US$ 300 Bn by 2035
- Local semiconductor production could meet more than 60% of domestic demand by 2035, requiring 20-25 OSAT facilities nationwide
- Global HDI PCB market projected to reach US$ 26.90 Bn by 2030 at a 10.9% CAGR; India's PCB industry expected to approach US$ 14 Bn by 2030 with roughly 88% of domestic PCB demand currently met through imports, creating a large import-substitution opening
- Global PCB assembly market projected to reach US$ 740 Bn by CY 2026 at a 4.4% CAGR from CY 2023, with consumer electronics and automotive dominating share
- India's grid digitisation under RDSS targeting deployment of over 250 Mn smart meters with a full software stack, creating a digital utility ecosystem of AMI, HES, MDM, analytics and grid intelligence platforms
- National rail investment scaling through 2030, with additional infrastructure projects worth Rs 1,364.45 Crores approved to accelerate Kavach deployment and an LTE communication backbone allocation estimated at over Rs 27,600 Crores; railway and transport outlays of nearly US$ 750 Bn by 2030 driving signalling, safety electronics and intelligent control demand
- Electrification of mobility: the Indian EV market projected to grow from US$ 3.98 Bn in 2024 to US$ 17.88 Bn by 2032 at a 19.0% CAGR, and Indian automotive electronics projected to reach US$ 19.2 Bn by 2034, raising PCBA content per vehicle
- Indian defence sector expected to generate electronics demand of approximately Rs 70-72 Bn over the next decade, supported by increasing localisation in design and manufacturing
- Convergence of AI, ML, IoT and cloud with 5G rollout, AI data centres and Industry 4.0 automation, structurally increasing demand for advanced electronic assemblies
- Transition towards high-mix, low-to-medium volume (HMLV) manufacturing in aerospace, industrial automation and medical devices, structurally favouring integrated ESDM players over high-volume mass producers
- Company-specific mix lever: automotive electronics currently contributes approximately 25% of total revenues, and the Company serves as a direct Tier 1 vendor to 10 different OEMs
- Anchor clients secured for the Sanand OSAT facility — Alpha & Omega Semiconductor (AOS), Infineon for MEMS-based True Wireless Stereo packaging, and L&T Semiconductor — with binding contractual arrangements that reinforce long-term revenue visibility for the facility
- In aerospace and defence, facilities have secured approvals and sizeable orders from major global OEMs, with the vertical scaling towards a target of 10% of total revenues
- Onboarded one of the world's Top 10 global Tier 1 automotive suppliers as a major client alongside India's largest two-wheeler EV manufacturers, with collaboration on upcoming two-, three- and four-wheeler models
- Kavach positioned against an estimated Rs 3,40,000 Mn Total Addressable Market co-developed with international technology partners

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Kaynes' FY 2025-26 expansion programme centred on two greenfield initiatives that moved from planning to execution. The Sanand OSAT facility was operationalised and delivered India's first commercially manufactured Multi-Chip Module (IPM5) in collaboration with global partners; the Company also received the Financial Support Agreement under the India Semiconductor Mission, giving visibility on central and state capital subsidies and improving cash-flow certainty. Total capex earmarked for OSAT is Rs 33,070 Mn, materially de-risked by the FSA, with eligible support of a 50% central subsidy and a 20% state subsidy on allowable capex of Rs 26,150 Mn. In parallel, the multilayer HDI PCB facility at Chennai is nearing completion and is designed to manufacture complex boards of up to 74 layers for defence, aerospace and strategic electronics applications; Phase 1 capex for the Chennai facility is Rs 14,000 Mn, described as government-approved capex targeted for South India, and is expected to unlock synergies between bare-board production and electronic system assembly. Together these position the Company to offer an integrated 'silicon-to-system' solution. Capital allocation in the core EMS business is deliberately selective — deployed for debottlenecking, focused on improving asset turnover, and avoiding a build-up of redundant capacity. The Company states it is adequately funded through internal accruals and previous QIP raises and does not intend to undertake further equity dilution to execute its immediate expansion phases. Footprint additions also came inorganically and through capability build-out: the integration of August Electronics in Canada established a credible manufacturing footprint in North America in RF microwave assemblies; a strategic collaboration with Infineon opened entry into MEMS-based True Wireless Stereo packaging; the Kochi plant runs high-volume manufacturing of client computing devices; and the Chamarajanagara plant participates in India's PARAM Supercomputer Mission through the high-end Rudra server. In the smart-utility business, GridCrest has deployed meter-to-cash solutions for about 2.50 Mn smart meters across Gujarat, Kerala, West Bengal, Nagaland and Madhya Pradesh, and its platform is described as globally scalable with planned entry into European markets.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident but cautious; acknowledged guidance misses; committed to execution discipline; emphasized transition from EMS to ESDM/product company; tone shifted from aggressive targets to sustainable, quality-led growth

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertical integration across the electronics value chain — HDI PCB substrate fabrication, core EMS assembly and OSAT semiconductor packaging — giving control over board architecture, component packaging and traceability, and reducing import dependence
- First-mover position in Indian semiconductor back-end: the Sanand OSAT facility delivered India's first commercially manufactured Multi-Chip Module (IPM5) and holds a Financial Support Agreement under the India Semiconductor Mission that gives visibility on central and state capital subsidies
- Design-led capability anchored by a DSIR-recognised R&D centre in Mysuru and dedicated design hubs; ODM, IoT and Product Engineering account for approximately 28% of total revenues
- Proprietary safety technology in the Kavach railway safety system, developed with international technology partners, in a programme with a projected addressable market of about Rs 3,40,000 Mn over five to seven years
- High switching costs from certification-heavy, high-entry-barrier sectors: an accreditation stack spanning IATF 16949, ISO 22163, ISO 13485, AS9100 and Nadcap supports aerospace, defence, railways and medical qualification
- Over three decades of operating experience and enduring relationships with global OEMs and Tier I suppliers across high-reliability sectors
- Geographically distributed Indian manufacturing footprint across Mysuru, Bengaluru, Manesar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Chamarajanagara, Pune and Sanand, equipped with advanced SMT and THT lines and cable harnessing capability, serving both high-mix low-volume and large-scale production
- Global footprint extended by the acquisition of Sensonic GmbH, Austria (rail electronics) and August Electronics in Canada (RF microwave assemblies and a manufacturing footprint in North America), offering customers a dependable near-shore alternative
- Operational excellence programme embedding Total Productive Maintenance, Poke-Yoke, MES and IoT 4.0 low-cost automation across sites, with internal compliance and audit review processes integrated in the ERP system

non_obvious.body: Metering business is 60% EMS legacy revenue — the 'new' revenue is only 40%; securitization progress is slow (only INR40cr done) due to installation delays, not bank reluctance; AI integration already live in 2 plants; board added ex-BEL CFO and ISRO expert — signals defense/space push

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve from a service-led EMS provider into a product-led, fully integrated ESDM architect that captures higher value across the electronics value chain
- Backward-integrate into bare-board PCB fabrication by establishing one of India's first advanced multilayer and HDI PCB manufacturing facilities at Chennai, producing complex boards of up to 74 layers for aerospace, defence, telecom, artificial intelligence, medical electronics, automotive, consumer electronics and industrial applications
- Extend PCB integration upstream through a secured Phase 2 government approval for South India enabling …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] Order book stated at Rs 89,038 Mn for Q1 FY27 against Rs 74,011 Mn for Q1 FY26 (deck's label: 'Order Book, INR Million').
- [Market context] Per KPMG's 'India's Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) Opportunity', the deck cites a global electronics market CAGR of 6.6% and a global EMS market CAGR of 6.6%, with the global EMS market's 2025 geographical share at APAC 68%, North America 18%, Europe 6%, Latin America 5% and MEA 3%.
- [Input cost inflation] The deck lists component price changes of 40-105% for DRAM & NAND, 15-85% for MCU & power devices, 15-60% for MLCCs & tantalum caps, 15-25% for chip resistors, 10-20% for diodes & MOSFETs and 5-30% for connectors - a direct margin risk for an EMS bill of materials.
- [Macro] Management flags rupee depreciation from ~85 in Jun 25 to ~96 in Jul 26 (down almost ~11%), making capital goods, spares and technology imports more expensive, and India WPI jumping to 9.68% in May 2026 with petroleum and natural gas prices up 61.5% YoY.
- [Basis of disclosure] Headline scale metrics are labelled 'Group Overview' and the financials are consolidated; the deck does not separate the listed entity from subsidiaries such as Kaynes Semicon, Kaynes Circuits, Digicom, August Electronics or Sensonic GmbH.
